extracted.intended_audience: users of PARI/GP (number_theorists, mathematicians, and programmers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions focused on arithmetic, factorization, elliptic curves, and number field utilities; lists function behavior, input type requirements, flags/options, limits, warnings, and library syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: divisors(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: creates a vector of the positive divisors of the integer x in increasing order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factorization of x (as output by factor) can be used instead. Library syntax: divisors(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: eulerphi(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Euler’s φ (totient) function of |x|, i.e. |(Z/xZ)^*|. x must be of type integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: phi(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: factor(x, {lim = −1})
rubrics_metrics.description: General factorization: if x is integer, rational, polynomial or rational function, returns a two-column matrix: irreducibles dividing x and their exponents. For vectors/matrices factoring is componentwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By definition 0 is factored as 0^1. For integer/rational x an optional lim restricts found factors up to lim or primelimit (lim=0 same as primelimit). Remaining part may be composite. Polynomials/rational functions must have scalar coefficients; PARI does not factor multivariate polynomials. Polynomial factorization is up to multiplication by a constant; content is discarded (use content(...) if needed). Library syntax: factor0(x, lim) where lim is a C integer; factor(x) = factor0(x,-1); smallfact(x) = factor0(x,0). See factornf for more.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorback(f, {nf})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given any factorization f, returns back the factored object. If nf is supplied, f is assumed to be a prime ideal factorization in the number field nf; the resulting ideal is given in HNF form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: factorback(f, nf), omitted nf is entered as NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorcantor(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using distinct degree plus Cantor–Zassenhaus. Coefficients must be compatible with Z/pZ. Result is two-column matrix: irreducible factors and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only degrees of irreducible polynomials are needed use factormod(x,p,1). factormod is usually faster. Library syntax: factorcantor(x,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorff(x, p, a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x in the field F_q defined by the irreducible polynomial a over F_p. Coefficients of x must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Returns two-column matrix of irreducibles and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to use for the variable of a a name distinct from other variables so lift() of the result is legible. Library syntax: factormod9(x,p,a).

rubrics_metrics.name: factorial(x) and x!
rubrics_metrics.description: Factorial of x. The expression x! gives an integer result; factorial(x) gives a real number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mpfact(x) for x! and mpfactr(x, prec) for factorial(x). x must be a long integer and not a PARI integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint(n, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors integer n using a combination of Pollard Rho (Brent), Lenstra ECM (Montgomery mods), and MPQS plus search for pure powers (exponents ≤ 10). Output is two-column matrix like factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives direct access to the integer factoring engine. flag is optional; binary digits: 1 avoid MPQS, 2 skip first stage ECM, 4 avoid Rho, 8 don't run final ECM (may declare huge composite prime). A strong probabilistic primality test is used (rare composites may pass). Machinery is experimental but faster on average at cost of memory; play with flags and use GP's debuglevel to watch internals. Library syntax: factorint(n, flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod(x, p, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors polynomial x modulo prime p using Berlekamp. Coefficients must be operation-compatible with Z/pZ. Result is two-column matrix of irreducible factors and exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag ≠ 0 outputs only the degrees of irreducible polynomials (useful for L-functions). factorcantor sometimes faster. Library syntax: factormod(x,p,flag). Also factormod(x,p) ≡ factormod(x,p,0) and simplefactormod(x,p) = factormod(x,p,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: fibonacci(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the x-th Fibonacci number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: fibo(x). x must be a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcd(x, y, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Greatest common divisor of x and y. Accepts general types including rationals, vectors/matrices (GCD taken recursively on components). Note: for vector/matrix types gcd is not necessarily commutative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0: Euclid's algorithm. flag=1: modular gcd algorithm (x,y must be polynomials with integer coefficients). flag=2: subresultant algorithm. Library syntax: gcd0(x,y,flag). Also ggcd(x,y) (flag=0), modulargcd(x,y) (flag=1), srgcd(x,y) (flag=2).

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbert(x, y, {p})
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert symbol of x and y modulo p. If x and y are integers/fractions, explicit third parameter p must be supplied (p=0 for the place at infinity). Otherwise p need not be given and x,y can be integer, fraction, real, integermod or p-adic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: hil(x,y,p).

rubrics_metrics.name: isfundamental(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x equals 1 or the discriminant of a quadratic field, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gisfundamental(x) but simpler isfundamental(x) returns a long and should be used if x is known to be of type integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprime(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a strong pseudoprime for 10 randomly chosen bases, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gisprime(x); the simpler isprime(x) returns a long and should be used if x is known to be an integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprime(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a strong pseudoprime for a randomly chosen base, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gispsp(x); simpler ispsp(x) returns a long and should be used if x is an integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: issquare(x, {&n})
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a square, false (0) if not. x can be any type. If n is given and an exact square root had to be computed, puts that root in n (especially for integers/polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not applicable for intmods (use quadratic reciprocity) or series (only check leading coefficient). Library syntax: carrecomplet(x,&n) or carreparfait(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: issquarefree(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is squarefree, false (0) otherwise. x can be integer or polynomial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gissquarefree(x); simpler issquarefree(x) returns a long for integer x. Computed as square of Moebius function, via multiplicative arithmetic methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: kronecker(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kronecker (generalized Legendre) symbol (x over y). x and y must be integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: kronecker(x,y), result is 0 or ±1 as a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: lcm(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Least common multiple of x and y, such that lcm(x,y)*gcd(x,y) = abs(x*y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: glcm(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: moebius(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Moebius µ-function of |x|. x must be an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mu(x). Result (0 or ±1) is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: nextprime(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds the smallest prime greater than or equal to x. Works for any real type; returns x if x is prime (not strictly larger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nextprime(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numdiv(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of divisors of |x|. x must be integer; result is a long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: numbdiv(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: omega(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of distinct prime divisors of |x|. x must be an integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: omega(x). Result is a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: precprime(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Finds the largest prime less than or equal to x. x can be any real type. Returns 0 if x ≤ 1. If x is prime returns x (not strictly smaller).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: precprime(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: prime(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: The x-th prime number, which must be among the precalculated primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: prime(x). x must be a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: primes(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a row vector whose components are the first x prime numbers, which must be among precalculated primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: primes(x). x must be a long.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbclassno(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Class number of the quadratic field of discriminant x. For x>0 current simple algorithm makes x not too large (say x < 10^7); for x<0 can compute |x| < 10^25 with Shanks’ method (O(|x|^{1/4})).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 computes class number using Euler products and functional equation (O(|x|^{1/2})). Warning: for D<0 this function often gives incorrect results when class group is non-cyclic because Shanks’ method incomplete; recommended to use version with flag=1, qfbclassno(-x) if x known fundamental, or quadclassunit for larger x. Library syntax: qfbclassno0(x,flag). Aliases: classno(x)=qfbclassno(x), classno2(x)=qfbclassno(x,1). Use hclassno(x) or qfbhclassno for other methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbcompraw(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of binary quadratic forms x and y without reduction of the result; useful to compute a generating element of an ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: compraw(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbhclassno(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz class number of x where x is non-negative and congruent to 0 or 3 mod 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See also qfbclassno. Library syntax: hclassno(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnucomp(x, y, l)
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms x and y using NUCOMP and NUDUPL algorithms of Shanks (à la Atkin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: l is any positive constant; optimal speed when l = |D|^{1/4} where D is common discriminant. Use nudupl(x,l) when x=y for speed. Library syntax: nucomp(x,y,l).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnupow(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of primitive positive definite binary quadratic form x using NUCOMP/NUDUPL algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: nupow(x,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbpowraw(x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of binary quadratic form x computed without reduction (using qfbcompraw). Here n must be non-negative and n < 2^31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: powraw(x,n) where n is a long integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbprimeform(x, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime binary quadratic form of discriminant x whose first coefficient is the prime p. Returns error if x is not a quadratic residue mod p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When x>0 the 'distance' component set equal to zero according to current precision. Library syntax: primeform(x,p,prec) (prec only used when x>0).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbred(x, {flag = 0}, {D}, {isqrtD}, {sqrtD})
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduces binary quadratic form x. flag controls behavior: 0 default uses Shanks' distance d; 1 uses d but single reduction step; 2 does not compute d; 3 does not use d and single reduction step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional D, isqrtD, sqrtD supply discriminant and related values (no checking done). If D<0 these values are useless. Library syntax: qfbred0(x,flag,D,isqrtD,sqrtD) using NULL to omit. Provided convenience aliases for definite/indefinite forms: redimag, redreal, rhoreal, redrealnod, rhorealnod.

rubrics_metrics.name: quadclassunit(D, {flag = 0}, {tech = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Buchmann–McCurley sub-exponential algorithm to compute class group of quadratic field of discriminant D. If D not fundamental function may or may not be defined (often gives right answer with warning). For orders use bnrinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instead of qfbclassno or quadregulator when D < −1025, D > 10^10, or when group structure is wanted. If flag non-zero and D>0 computes narrow class group (current version may not work; use bnfnarrow). Optional tech = [c1,c2] control execution time and stack size. For maximum speed set c2=c; to get rigorous result under GRH set c2=6. Reasonable c values between 0.1 and 2. Result vector v has components: v[1]=class number; v[2]=structure as product of cyclic groups; v[3]=generators; v[4]=regulator (omitted if D<0); v[5]=measure of correctness (close to 1 is correct under GRH; if close to larger integer class number off by that factor — increase c1 or change seed). Library syntax: quadclassunit0(D,flag,tech). Aliases: buchimag(D,c1,c2), buchreal(D,flag,c1,c2).

rubrics_metrics.name: quaddisc(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discriminant of the quadratic field Q(sqrt(x)) where x ∈ Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: quaddisc(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadhilbert(D, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation defining Hilbert class field of quadratic field of discriminant D. If flag non-zero and D<0 outputs [form, root(form)] (for constructing subfields). Uses complex multiplication in imaginary case and Stark units in real case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: quadhilbert(D,flag,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadgen(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates quadratic number ω = (a + sqrt(x))/2 where a=0 if x≡0 mod 4, a=1 if x≡1 mod4, so (1, ω) is integral basis for quadratic order of discriminant x. x must be integer congruent to 0 or 1 modulo 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: quadgen(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadpoly(D, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates canonical quadratic polynomial (in variable v) corresponding to discriminant D, i.e. minimal polynomial of quadgen(x). D must be integer congruent to 0 or 1 mod 4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: quadpoly0(x,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadray(D, f, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative equation for ray class field of conductor f for quadratic field of discriminant D (or bnf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For D<0 flag semantics: odd integer flag outputs vector of [ideal, corresponding root]; flag=0 or 1 uses σ function, flag>1 uses Weierstrass ℘ (less efficient and partially implemented). flag can be [λ,flag] where λ is technical element needed for Schertz’s method; returns 0 if λ unsuitable. For D>0 if flag non-zero try to get simplest modulus (see bnrstark); function may fail with 'Cannot find a suitable modulus in FindModulus'. Library syntax: quadray(D,f,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadregulator(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulator of quadratic field of positive discriminant x. Returns error if x is not a discriminant or if x is a square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large x see quadclassunit. Library syntax: regula(x,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: quadunit(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental unit of real quadratic field Q(sqrt(x)) where x is positive discriminant of the field. If x not fundamental discriminant, probably gives fundamental unit of corresponding order. x must be integer; result is a quadratic number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: fundunit(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: removeprimes({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes the primes listed in x from the prime number table. If x omitted lists current extra primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular removeprimes(addprimes) empties the extra prime table. x can be a single integer. Library syntax: removeprimes(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: sigma(x, {k = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of the k-th powers of the positive divisors of |x|. x must be integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: sumdiv(x) (= sigma(x)) or gsumdivk(x,k) (= sigma(x,k)) where k is a C long integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: sqrtint(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer square root of x where x must be PARI type integer. Result non-negative and rounded towards zero. Negative x allowed: result is I*sqrtint(-x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: racine(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: znlog(x, g)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete logarithm of x to base g where g must be primitive root mod prime p. Uses baby-step/giant-step requiring O(sqrt(p)) storage; cannot be used for p greater than about 10^13 due to storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: znlog(x,g).

rubrics_metrics.name: znorder(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of x in multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^*. x must be invertible mod n; returns error if not invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: order(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: znprimroot(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a primitive root of x where x is a prime power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: gener(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: znstar(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives structure of multiplicative group (Z/nZ)^* as a 3-component row vector v: v[1]=φ(n) order, v[2]=k-component row-vector d of integers with d[i]>1 and d[i] | d[i-1] giving decomposition, v[3]=generators for image of cyclic groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: znstar(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: elliptic_curve_section_conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions for elliptic curve functions: curve given by Weierstrass model y^2 + a1 x y + a3 y = x^3 + a2 x^2 + a4 x + a6, represented as 5-component vector E=[a1,a2,a3,a4,a6]. Points as [x,y], identity [0]. ellinit gives a long (19) or medium (13) vector with fixed data; many member names (a1–a6, b2–b8, c4–c6, area, disc, j, omega, eta, roots, tate, w) available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ellinit to compute fixed curve data; long vector (~19 components) contains more data including periods/quasi-periods for curves over Q and p-adic data for Qp. Some functions require curve to be in minimal Weierstrass form (use ellglobalred). All ell- functions take the curve as first argument in one of the formats described.

rubrics_metrics.name: elladd(E, z1, z2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sum of points z1 and z2 on elliptic curve corresponding to vector E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: addell(E,z1,z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellak(E, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes coefficient a_n of L-function of elliptic curve E (coefficients of newform of weight 2 assuming modularity). E must be medium or long vector from ellinit; for every n and not just those prime to conductor, E must be a minimal Weierstrass equation (use ellglobalred if needed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: akell(E,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellan(E, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes vector of first n a_k coefficients for elliptic curve E. Same requirements as ellak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: anell(E,n) where n is C integer.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellap(E, p, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a_p given by #E(F_p) = p + 1 − a_p. For flag=0 uses baby-step giant-step + Mestre trick (O(p^{1/4}) time/storage, impractical when p has ~30 digits). flag=1 computes a_p as sum of Legendre symbols (slower when p>~100). No primality check on p. E must be medium/long vector, defined over Q, Fp, or Qp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ellap0(E,p,flag). Aliases: apell(E,p) (flag=0), apell2(E,p) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellbil(E, z1, z2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes canonical bilinear form on z1, z2: ellheight(E,z1+z2) - ellheight(E,z1) - ellheight(E,z2). z1 or z2 (but not both) can be vectors/matrices. Equals twice some normalizations. E assumed integral, minimal model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: bilhell(E,z1,z2,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangecurve(E, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes curve coordinates using vector v=[u,r,s,t] via x = u^2 x' + r, y = u^3 y' + s u^2 x' + t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E must be medium or long vector from ellinit. Library syntax: coordch(E,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellchangepoint(x, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes coordinates of point or vector of points x using v=[u,r,s,t] with same coordinate change formula as ellchangecurve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: pointch(x,v). See also ellchangecurve.

rubrics_metrics.name: elleisnum(E, k, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given elliptic curve E (ellinit output or lattice [ω1,ω2]) and even positive integer k, computes numerical value of Eisenstein series of weight k at E. If flag non-zero and k=4 or 6 returns g2 or g3 with correct normalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: elleisnum(E,k,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: elleta(om)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns two-component row vector [η1, η2] of quasi-periods associated to om=[ω1,ω2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: elleta(om,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellglobalred(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculates arithmetic conductor, global minimal model of E, and global Tamagawa number c. E must be medium/long vector from ellinit and have ai in Q. Result [N,v,c] where N is arithmetic conductor, v=[u,r,s,t] coordinate change giving integral everywhere-minimal model with normalization a1∈{0,1}, a2∈{0,±1}, a3∈{0,1} (unique with u>0), and c product of local Tamagawa numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get new model type ellchangecurve(E,v). Library syntax: globalreduction(E).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheight(E, z, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Global Néron–Tate height of point z on elliptic curve E. E must be a long vector from ellinit; with flag=0 uses sigma and theta-functions and Silverman trick; flag=1 uses Tate's 4n algorithm (much slower). E assumed integral, minimal model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ellheight0(E,z,flag,prec). Archimedean contribution given by hell(E,z,prec). Aliases: ghell(E,z,prec) (flag=0), ghell2(E,z,prec) (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellheightmatrix(E, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector x of points outputs Gram matrix with respect to Néron–Tate height: (i,j) entry = ellbil(E,x[i],x[j]). Rank (approximately) gives rank of set; determinant equals regulator if x basis of Mordell–Weil group. Note matrix should be divided by 2 to match some normalizations. E assumed integral, minimal model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: mathell(E,x,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellinit(E, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes fixed data for elliptic curve given by five-component vector E; result is 19-component 'long' vector or 13-component 'medium' vector if flag=1. First 13 components present in both: a1,a2,a3,a4,a6,b2,b4,b6,b8,c4,c6,Δ,j (discriminant E[12], j-invariant E[13]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remaining six components present only if flag=0 and depend on base field: over R includes roots (E[14]), real/complex periods (E[15],E[16]), quasi-periods (E[17],E[18]), area (E[19]); over Qp includes p-adic root, u^2,u,q values and w; other fields set to zero. Library syntax: ellinit0(E,flag,prec). Aliases: initell(E,prec) (flag=0) and smallinitell(E,prec) (flag=1). Member retrieval via E.disc, E.j, E.omega, E.eta etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellisoncurve(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 1 if point z is on elliptic curve E, 0 otherwise. If E or z have imprecise coefficients an imprecise equality is checked rather than exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: oncurve(E,z) returns long.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellj(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elliptic j-invariant. x must be complex with positive imaginary part or convertible into a power series or p-adic number with positive valuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: jell(x,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllocalred(E, p)
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculates Kodaira type of local fiber of elliptic curve E at prime p. E must be medium/long vector from ellinit and have ai in Z. Result [f,kod,v,c]: f exponent of p in arithmetic conductor, kod Kodaira type encoded (1=I0 good, 2=II,3=III,4=IV, 4+ν with ν>0 is Iν; negative values refer to starred types), v=[u,r,s,t] giving coordinate changes, c local Tamagawa number cp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: localreduction(E,p). Normally v useless if u=1 (equation already minimal).

rubrics_metrics.name: elllseries(E, s, {A = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes value of L-series of E at s. E must be minimal over Z and a modular elliptic curve. Optional A is cutoff for integral (choose near 1 for speed); result must be independent of A as internal check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conductor large (e.g. >10^12) function is impractical (uses O(N^{1/2}) algorithm). Library syntax: lseriesell(E,s,A,prec) where omitted A coded as NULL.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellorder(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives order of point z on curve E if torsion point, zero otherwise. Implemented only for curves over Q in current version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: orderell(E,z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellordinate(E, x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns 0,1 or 2-component vector containing y-coordinates of points of E with given x-coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ordell(E,x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpointtoz(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E has coefficients in R computes complex number t (mod lattice) corresponding to point z so that ℘(t)=z[1], ℘'(t)=z[2]; inverse of ellztopoint. For Qp-case returns p-adic t via Tate parametrization (or t+1/t if only u^2 in Qp). E must be a long vector from ellinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: zell(E,z,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellpow(E, z, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes n times point z under group law on elliptic curve E. n can be integer; can also be complex quadratic integer if E has complex multiplication by n (error otherwise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: powell(E,z,n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellrootno(E, {p = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes local (if p≠1) or global (if p=1) root number of L-series of E. Global root number is sign of functional equation and conjecturally parity of Mordell–Weil rank. Equation for E must have coefficients in Q but need not be minimal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ellrootno(E,p). Result ±1 as long.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsigma(E, z, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of Weierstrass σ function of lattice associated to E (ellinit) or given lattice [ω1,ω2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 compute determination of log(σ(z)); flag=2,3 use product expansion instead of theta series. Library syntax: ellsigma(E,z,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellsub(E, z1, z2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Difference of points z1 and z2 on elliptic curve E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: subell(E,z1,z2).

rubrics_metrics.name: elltaniyama(E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes modular parametrization of elliptic curve E (given by ellinit) as two-component vector [u,v] of power series to current default series precision. Characterized by (u,v) satisfying curve equation and du/(2v+a1u+a3) = f(z)dz for f a form on H/Γ0(N). Variable in series is x=exp(2iπz). Assumes E is strong Weil curve and Manin constant =1. Equation must be minimal (use ellglobalred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: taniyama(E). Precision determined by global precdl.

rubrics_metrics.name: elltors(E, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: For E over Q outputs torsion subgroup as [t,v1,v2] where t is order, v1 structure as product of cyclic groups (sorted), v2 generators. E must be long vector from ellinit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided. flag=0 uses Doud's algorithm (bound torsion via #E(Fp) for small primes then look for torsion points using Weierstrass parametrization and Mazur's classification). flag=1 uses Lutz–Nagell (much slower) and allows medium vector. Library syntax: elltors0(E,flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellwp(E, {z = x}, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes Weierstrass ℘ function value at z for lattice attached to E or returns power series expansion in z when z omitted or variable (starts z^{-2}+O(z^2)). Number of terms given by default serieslength or second arg in library mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag only used when z numeric: 0 compute ℘(z) only; 1 compute [℘(z), ℘'(z)]. Library syntax: ellwp0(E,z,flag,prec,precdl). Alias weipell(E,precdl) for power series.

rubrics_metrics.name: ellzeta(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of Weierstrass ζ function of the lattice associated to E (ellinit) or given lattice [ω1,ω2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: ellzeta(E,z).

rubrics_metrics.name: ellztopoint(E, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given long vector E computes coordinates [x,y] on E corresponding to complex number z (Weierstrass ℘ and derivative). Inverse of ellpointtoz. If z in lattice returns point at infinity [0].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: pointell(E,z,prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: number_field_conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions for functions related to general number fields: nf is a 9-component vector from nfinit containing signature, maximal order, discriminant, etc.; bnf is 10-component vector from bnfinit with deeper invariants (units, class groups) used by complex functions; bnr is 'big ray number field' from bnrinit; rnf denotes a relative number field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of 'ideal' is given: can be a Z-basis in HNF or not (square matrix) etc. These conventions apply to subsequent functions in section 3.6.
